newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi Hutu group kills at least 26 - witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Burundi Hutu group kills at least 26 - witnesses.

text.p: Hutu rebels killed at least 26 Hutu civilians in Burundi's troubled northwestern province of Cibitoke, witnesses said.

Rebels from the Party for the Liberation of the Hutu People (Palipehutu) killed people at Cibitoke's Buhindo zone, Murwi commune, 80 km (50 miles) north of the capital Bujumbura, between July 2 and 6, according to witnesses who fled Buhindo and spoke to reporters on Monday.
Around 2,500 people fled Buhindo to Buhinyuza, Rugombo commune, where the army set up a camp for them.

"It all started on July 2 and I can confirm that on that day the rebels killed 26 people who were trying to flee Buhindo zone. I don't know the exact number of people killed because other corpses were thrown in the Muhira river," said Nestor Mpawenimana, Buhindo zone chief who fled his post. Other villagers confirmed the story.

"We fled because there was the presence of lots of Palipehutu who took our goods. We were afraid to die unjustly when the army started its operation there," villager Jackson Nsekambagbaye told independent production Studio Ijambo.

Burundi's army said 214 rebels were killed in Murwi commune during a battle between the armed wing of the main Hutu rebel group the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) and Palipehutu.
Soldiers in Cibitoke and villagers disputed the account, but did not say what prompted the intra-ethnic killings.
"We know that 214 assailants have been killed in combat between different armed Hutu factions in Murwi around July 2," said army spokesman Colonel Mamert Sinarinzi.

Jerome Ndiho, CNDD spokesman contacted in Brussels, said he knew nothing about the killings, adding that Palipehutu was a spent force and last fought CNDD in 1995. It was not possible to contact Palipehutu for comment.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi since October 1993, when the country's first freely elected Hutu president, Melchior Ndadaye, was murdered in an attempted army coup.
CNDD, established in April 1995, has become the main armed Hutu opposition, usurping the much older Palipehutu.
Burundi military leader Pierre Buyoya announced last week he would start direct talks between his government and CNDD towards a ceasefire.
